question.text:
Which of the following theorems can solve all Recurrence Relations?

  1. Mater Tehorem
  2. Akra-Bazzi Theorem
  3. Both [A] and [B]
  4. Akra-Bazzi can be applied to some cases but not for all.

Find the time complexity of the function

function( int n)
{
    int i=1;
    while( i<n)
    {
        int j=n;
        while( j>0)
            j=j/2;
            i=2*i;
    }
}
  1. $O(\log n)$
  2. $O(n^2 \log n )$
  3. $O(\log 2 n)$
  4. $O( \log n^2 )$

Which of the following algorithms CANNOT be designed without recursion?

  1. Tower of Hanoi
  2. Fibonacci Series
  3. Tree Traversal
  4. None of the above

What will be the running-time of Dijkstra's single source shortest path algorithm, if the graph $G(V,E)$ is stored in the form of an adjacency list and binary heap is used?

  1. $O (\mid V \mid 2)$
  2. $O (\mid V \mid \log \mid V \mid)$
  3. $O ( ( \mid E \mid+\mid V \mid ) \log \mid V \mid )$
  4. $O( \log \mid V \mid )$

A problem called Boolean Parenthesis Matching (match all parenthesis in an expression) can be solved by:

  1. Greedy Approach
  2. Recursion
  3. Dynamic Approach
  4. Both [B] and [C]

$O(n^k)$ is complexity of the best method that finds longest Palindrome Substring in a word. For example, in the word "Atatb", the longest palindrome string is "tat". Then, the value of $10^*K$ is __________.

Which of the following statements is FALSE?

  1. Optimal binary search tree construction can be performed efficiently using dynamic programming.
  2. Breadth-first search cannot be used to find connected components of a graph.
  3. Given the prefix and postfix walks of a binary tree, the tree cannot be re-constructed uniquely.
  4. Depth-first-search can be used to find the components of a graph.

Assume that the splits at every level of Quick-Sort are in proportion $1-p$ to $p$, where $p (0 < p \leq 0.5 )$ is a constant.  The number of elements in an array is $n$. The maximum depth is approximately:

  1. $0.5 \ p \ \text{lg } n$
  2. $0.5 \ (1 - p) \ \text{lg } n$
  3. $p (\text{lg }n) / (\text{lg }p)$
  4. $- (\text{lg }n) / \text{lg }(1 - p)$

Linked Lists are not suitable for :

  1. Binary Search
  2. Polynomial Manipulation
  3. Insertion
  4. Radix Sort

In Strassen's Matrix Multiplication, what is the number of additions and multiplications done to get a better complexity than the normal matrix multiplication?

  1. $7$ and $16$
  2. $18$ and $7$
  3. $10$ and $8$
  4. $7$ and $7$

In order to construct the Minimum Spanning Tree, which of the following options represents the correct order of edges in which they are added to construct the tree?

  1. $4,2,1,7,10$
  2. $4,2,1,6,8$
  3. $4,1 ,2,8,10$
  4. $4,1,2,6,8$

The time complexity of the function mentioned below is:

void f(int k[], int n)
{
int i;
printf("%d",n);
for(i=0; i<n; i++)
{
printf("%d",k[i]);
}
printf("n");
}
  1. $O(n^2)$
  2. $O(n \log n)$
  3. $O(n)$
  4. $O(n^3)$

Which one of the following is a topological sort for the above graph?

  1. $1, 6, 2, 5, 3, 4$
  2. $4, 5, 6, 3, 2, 1$
  3. $2, 4, 5, 6, 3, 1$
  4. $6, 4, 5, 2, 1, 3$

Match the following:
$\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|} \hline (1) & \text{Multistage graph} & (P) & \text{Divide and conquer}\\ \hline (2) & \text{Convex hull } & (Q) & \text{Depth first search} \\ \hline (3) & \text{Bi-connected components} & (R) & \text{Greedy method} \\ \hline (4) & \text{Knapsack problem} & (S) & \text{Dynamic programming} \\ \hline (5) & \text{All pairs shortest path} & \text{}\\\hline \end{array}$    

  1. 1 – Q, 2 – P, 3 – Q,  4– R,  5 – S
  2. 1 - Q,  2 - R, 3 - Q,  4 - P,  5 – S
  3. 1 - S,  2 – R, 3 - Q,  4– R,  5 – S
  4. 1 - S,  2 - P,  3 – Q,  4– R,  5 – S
The length of the longest common subsequence of $L = ( 1,0,0,1,0,1,0,1 )$ and  $K =( 0,1,0,1,1,0,1,1,0 )$ is __________.

Consider the following max-heap as given below :
        
       9
   /      \
  6        8
 / \      / \
3  4     5  7

The number of swaps required to convert the given max-heap into min-heap is ______.

Which of the following are TRUE?

  1. $n! = \theta ((n + 1)!)$
  2. $\log4 n   = \theta ( \log2 n  )$
  3. $\sqrt{\log n} = O(\log \log n)$
  1. (i) & (iii) only
  2. (i) & (ii) only
  3. (ii) only
  4. (i),(ii) and (iii)

The following elements are inserted in sequence to create an AVL tree: $31, 36, 40, 19, 14, 24, 50$

What is the pre-order traversal of the created AVL tree?

  1. $36, 19, 14, 31, 24, 40, 50$
  2. $36, 14, 19, 31, 24, 40, 50$
  3. $31, 19, 14, 24, 40, 36, 50$
  4. $31, 19, 14, 24, 36, 40, 50$

A hash table of length $7$ uses open addressing with hash function $h(k) = k \text{mod }7$ and linear probing to resolve collisions.

After inserting 6 values in an empty hash table, the table is shown below:

$\begin{array}{|c|c|} \hline 0 & 49 \\ \hline 1 & 35 \\ \hline 2 & 28 \\ \hline 3 & 16 \\ \hline 4 & {} \\ \hline 5 & 75 \\ \hline 6 & 89 \\ \hline \end{array}$

Which of the following insertion sequences can’t result in the above table ?

  1. $49,35,75,89,28,16$
  2. $49,28,35,16,75,89$
  3. $75,49,35,89,28,16$
  4. $49,35,28,75,16,89$

The number of comparisons required to find the maximum and minimum element in an array $A[n]$ using Divide and Conquer method is:

  1. $(3n/2)+ 2$
  2. $(3n/2) - 2$
  3. $3n$

Consider the following table :

$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline X & A & B & C & D \\ \hline Y & 14 & 3 & 6 & 10 \\ \hline \end{array}$

Here, X represents character and Y represents frequency.

The total number of bits needed to encode a string which has $14$ a's, $3$ b's, $6$ c's and $10$ d's using Huffman Code is _______.

Matrix multiplication is associative and MCS ( matrix chain multiplication ) uses the following matrices:

$\begin{array} \text{M1} & 10^* 100 \\ M2 & 100^* 5 \\ M3 &  5^* 50 \\ M4 & 50^* 1 \end{array}$

The number of orderings that are possible to compute $M1 \ M2 \ M3 \ M4$ are _________.

Given $n$ number of linearly ordered distinct elements, what will be the worst case time complexity to find

$p$-th smallest element $(1 \leq p \leq n)$ from these $n$ elements when $n > 50$?

  1. $O(n \log n)$
  2. $O(n^2)$
  3. $O(n)$
  4. $O(\log n)$
Let $T$ be a rooted ternary tree where each internal node of $T$ has a maximum of $3$ children. If root is at depth $0$, then maximum total number of vertices $T$ can have with depth $3$ is ______.

Consider the following instance of the knapsack problem :

$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline \text{Item} & a & b & c & d & e \\ \hline \text{Benefit} & 15 & 12 & 9 & 16 & 17 \\ \hline \text{Weight} & 2 & 5 & 3 & 4 & 6 \\ \hline \end{array}$

Maximum weight of knapsack is $12$. For the above weights and benefits of items, if we need an optimal solution of fractional knapsack problem, the value of maximum benefit will be ______.
The total number of LCS (Longest Common Subsequences) of $P = abcd123$  and $Q= badc321$ that can be formed are ______.

Assume Dijkstra's Algorithm is used to find the shortest paths from node G in the above graph. The total number of edges which are not included in any of the shortest paths from node G are  _________.

The given input sequence is $\{ 111, 333 , 243, 199, 234, 279, 119 \}$ and the hash table is of size $10$ with hash function $h(k) = k \mod 10$. When hash table uses quadratic probing with $h'(k)=  h(k) + c_1 * i + c_2 * i^2, c_1 = 0, c_2 = 1$, the total number of collisions happening while mapping the given input sequence are __________.

The cost of optimal binary search tree for the identifier set $(a1, a2, a3) =$ (do, if, while) with $p(1) = 0.3,  \ p(2) = 0.2, $ $p(3) = 0.15, q (0) = 0.05,  q(1) = 0.15, q(2)= 0.1, q(3) = 0.05$ is:

  1. $1.65$
  2. $1.95$
  3. $1.8$
  4. $2.1$
